title: Winged-Edge Mesh
author: Karsten Schmidt (toxi / postspectacular, 2010)
description: A half-edge / winged-edge data structure for triangle meshes, designed for sub-million-triangle scenes where simple flat vertex/index arrays become cumbersome. Each edge stores pointers to its two endpoint vertices, its two opposite edges (the 'wings'), and the two incident faces; traversal from edge to edge is a single pointer-deref. Karsten's toxiclibs.geom.WingedEdge class was the first Java implementation aimed at creative-coding scenes and ships a `computeVertexNormals()`, `subdivide()` (Catmull-Clark style on a triangle mesh via Loop subdivision), and an adjacency-iterator used by his subdivision demo. The structure prefigures the half-edge meshes later popularised by libraries like OpenMesh and libigl, and is the canonical example of an adjacency-graph data structure for a creative-coding context.
math_essence: For each triangle (v0, v1, v2), three directed edges e0=(v0,v1), e1=(v1,v2), e2=(v2,v0). For each edge, find the opposite edge in the adjacent triangle (if any) and link them. Vertex normals: average the cross products of the two outgoing edges of every face incident to the vertex. Subdivide: each triangle becomes 4 by inserting midpoint vertices on each edge (new vertex position = (v_a + v_b) / 2 for non-shared edges, or Loop-weighted blend for shared ones). The data structure supports O(1) vertex-to-face and face-to-edge traversal.
